html:
The Hammonasset were a small Algonquian people of the Connecticut coast, around the Hammonasset River between today's Madison and Clinton, east of New Haven. They were close to the Quinnipiac to the west.

They fished, gathered shellfish on the shore and grew maize. In the 1630s and 1640s English settlers moved onto the coast after the Pequot War, and the Hammonasset sold their lands to them. Many joined the Mohegan under the sachem Uncas. Little else is recorded of them; a beach and state park now carry their name.
